title: Footprints: The Making of a Scientist

topics.title: Richard Ebright: the making of a scientist

learn.hook: A boy who couldn't stop collecting butterflies grew up to study how living cells work.
points: 'The Making of a Scientist' by Robert W. Peterson tells the story of Richard H. Ebright, an American scientist who began by collecting butterflies as a child.
His mother encouraged him strongly; she gave him the book 'The Travels of Monarch X', which led him to tag monarch butterflies for research.
Through school science-fair projects, such as testing whether viceroy butterflies copy monarchs, he learnt to ask questions and test them.
As a college student, he and a friend worked out a theory of how cells read their DNA.
The lesson names three things that make a scientist: a first-rate mind, curiosity, and the will to win for the right reasons.

example.q: Think it through: Ebright's first science-fair project did not win. What did he learn from that, as a scientist would?
steps: Losing showed him that just displaying things was not enough.
He began doing real experiments that test a question.
So failure pushed him to improve instead of giving up.
example.answer: That science means asking a question and testing it with experiments; a setback is a chance to improve.

learn.reallife: Indian scientists like C.V. Raman and A.P.J. Abdul Kalam also began with a childhood curiosity about the world around them.

games.title: Ebright's journey
items: Develops a theory of how cells read DNA in college

quiz.q: Which insects fascinated Richard Ebright as a child?
Which book did his mother give Ebright?
quiz.explain: This book about monarch migration started his tagging work.
quiz.mistake: Picks a famous book from other lessons

quiz.q: Who encouraged Ebright the most as a child?
quiz.explain: His mother took him on trips and bought him science books and equipment.

quiz.q: What did Ebright's viceroy butterfly project test?
quiz.explain: He tested the theory that viceroys copy (mimic) monarchs.
quiz.mistake: Remembers the insect but not the question

quiz.q: Which is one quality the lesson says makes a scientist?
quiz.explain: The lesson lists a first-rate mind, curiosity, and the will to win for the right reasons.

quiz.q: What is the adjective form of 'science'?
quiz.explain: 'Scientist' is a person (noun); 'scientific' is the adjective.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the person noun with the adjective

quiz.explain: To mimic is to copy something's look or behaviour.
quiz.mistake: Guesses from context without knowing the word
Confuses the word with an unrelated feeling

teach.ask: Gappu: How did a boy who collected butterflies become a real scientist? What do I need to be one?
teach.praise: Science-chirp! Curiosity, experiments and encouragement. I'm starting my feather-collection research!
teach.nudge: Which quality made him ask questions? And how did he test his ideas?

topics.title: Curiosity in numbers: the analytical paragraph

learn.hook: Data tells a story too. Can you read it like a scientist?
points: Curious people ask 'why' and 'what if', then look at evidence, often in the form of data.
An analytical paragraph describes data from a chart or table in about 100-150 words.
Structure: introduction (what the data shows), body (main trends with exact figures and comparisons), conclusion (overall picture).
Trend words: rose/increased, fell/decreased, peaked (reached its highest), remained steady, fluctuated (rose and fell), doubled.
Use the past tense for past data, quote figures accurately, and do not add personal opinions not shown by the data.

example.q: Data: Science club members at Sunrise School: 2021: 20, 2022: 28, 2023: 35, 2024: 33, 2025: 50. Write an opening sentence and one trend sentence.
steps: Opening: say what the data is about and the period.
Trend: membership went from 20 to 35 between 2021 and 2023.
Then it fell slightly to 33 before rising to 50 in 2025.
example.answer: The chart shows science club membership at Sunrise School from 2021 to 2025. Membership rose from 20 to 35 by 2023, dipped slightly to 33 in 2024 and peaked at 50 in 2025.

learn.reallife: Reports on rainfall, cricket scores, and school results all use analytical writing to explain numbers.

quiz.q: Data: Science club members at Sunrise School: 2021: 20, 2022: 28, 2023: 35, 2024: 33, 2025: 50. In which year was membership the highest?
quiz.explain: 50 members in 2025 is the highest figure.
quiz.mistake: Picks the year before the small dip

quiz.q: Data: Science club members at Sunrise School: 2021: 20, 2022: 28, 2023: 35, 2024: 33, 2025: 50. By how many members did the club grow from 2021 to 2025?
quiz.mistake: Gives the final number instead of the increase

quiz.q: Data: Science club members at Sunrise School: 2021: 20, 2022: 28, 2023: 35, 2024: 33, 2025: 50. In which year did membership fall?
quiz.explain: It went from 35 in 2023 down to 33 in 2024.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare each year with the one before

quiz.explain: To double is to become two times as much.

quiz.q: How should an analytical paragraph begin?
options: With an introduction saying what the data is about
quiz.explain: The opening tells the reader what the chart shows and the period.

quiz.q: Which sentence best suits an analytical paragraph?
options: I think the science club is the best club ever.
Membership rose steadily from 20 in 2021 to 35 in 2023.
Everyone should join the science club!
The club is quite big, I guess.
quiz.explain: It describes a trend with exact figures, with no opinion.
Fluctuating figures go up and down.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it means a steady change

options: Why do the leaves of the touch-me-not plant fold when touched?
quiz.explain: It asks 'why' about a natural event and can be investigated.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any question shows scientific curiosity

teach.ask: Gappu: My teacher gave me a bar chart and said 'write an analytical paragraph'. Where do I even start?
teach.praise: Chart-chirp! Intro, trends with figures, and a conclusion. I can read data like a scientist!
teach.nudge: What do you say first about the chart? And do you use the actual numbers?
